statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk of 13% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold.
recommendation: Conditions are described as balanced and two-sided. The narrow flagged window runs from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC (15:30-17:00 Berlin), covering the U.S. cash open and the Richmond Fed and Fed-speaker cluster, with secondary conditional checkpoints at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and in the 19:00 UTC closing hour. Stress is moderate rather than low, so wider-than-usual intraday ranges are plausible without the price path itself turning one-way. Geopolitical headline risk around the UN General Assembly is an additional source of overnight gap risk.
headline: Record Nasdaq close digested in a flat overnight tape as crude turns back up on Iran tension
body: Nasdaq-100 cash closed Monday at a record 30,482.35, up 2.83% in its best session since early August, led by an AI chip surge after the reception of Meta's Muse assistant: Arm rose about 17%, Intel about 12%, AMD about 10% through a $1 trillion market capitalisation, Qualcomm more than 9% and Meta about 11%. Sector breadth was strongly aligned, with technology, communication services and semiconductor groups all higher. Falling crude and softer Treasury yields added support, the 10-year easing to about 4.96% from 5.02% highs last week. Overnight the front NQ contract traded up about 0.37% in Asia, as Reuters reported, then gave the move back in full; it now sits near 30,782, roughly flat against the prior settle, inside a 30,765.50-30,916.50 range. That completed round trip is the single most important current observation: it shows retracements occurring rather than a no-pullback extension, and with VIX at 14.87 the conditions under which mean reversion fails are not in evidence. Against that, crude has turned higher on Tuesday, Brent back above $100 and WTI firmer, after the U.S. Treasury Secretary said all Iranian airlines would be shut down from 23 September, reversing part of Monday's de-escalation-driven decline. That keeps an energy and geopolitical channel open through UN General Assembly week without so far transmitting into index futures. The rate path is the other standing tension: the dollar index is near a seven-week high at 100.4 and traders price roughly a 56% chance of an October hike, up from 43.5% a week earlier, so a record-high equity tape sits against a tightening policy backdrop. Tail is therefore held in the low band at 13% while Stress is carried at 39%, with conditional risk concentrated in the U.S. cash open and the scheduled afternoon checkpoints rather than spread across the session.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover a strongly directional U.S. session followed by a calm overnight. From 07:00 UTC on 21 September the mode was trend-up as European and then U.S. buyers extended the AI chip advance; Tail climbed from 12 to a 33 peak at 19:00 UTC while the Nasdaq-100 ran to a 2.83% record close at 30,482.35. After the 20:00 UTC cash close volatility decayed quickly, Tail fell to 14 within an hour and to 12 within two, and the mode reverted to normal from 22:00 UTC. The overnight stretch has been consistently two-sided, with Tail held between 11 and 13 and Stress between 32 and 36, and the Asian advance of about 0.37% was fully retraced by the end of the window.
outlookSummary: The base case for the next 24 hours is a two-way tape with conditional risk concentrated in the U.S. cash session. Tail is projected to hold the low band through Europe, cross the watch threshold at the 13:30 UTC cash open, peak at 24 during the 14:00 UTC Richmond Fed and Fed-speaker cluster, ease through early afternoon, and re-cross at the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction and again in the 19:00 UTC closing hour before decaying after the 20:00 UTC close. The overnight stretch into 23 September is projected in the low band at 13 to 15, lifting slightly at the end of the horizon ahead of that day's flash PMI release. No projection assumes that an unobserved future price path has already formed; the conditional peak stays below the block threshold because the identified amplifiers are scheduled and anticipated rather than observed.
